confidence_notes: I did two of the six allowed web searches: one for the RBA rate and one for Byron Bay cost-of-living sites (nomad.watch, jobicy, livingcost.org, citycost.org, expatexchange). Those sites gave rough ranges: cappuccino about A$4.50-5.50, inexpensive meal about A$18-25, mid-range three-course dinner for two about A$73-112, and a local draught beer anywhere from about A$8 to A$11.50. The sources disagree, some figures are crowdsourced and some are older, so I set the food and drink anchors at the upper middle of these ranges for a tourist area. Cocktail and wine prices are not from search; I estimated them from how they usually compare with beer in Australian bars and restaurants. That makes them less certain. All four accommodation anchors are my own estimates from general knowledge of Byron Bay. July is a cooler, quieter month, but rooms in Byron Bay are expensive all year and prices swing widely. I did not search for or check any accommodation prices, so accommodation is the least reliable part of this estimate.
comparable_city_reasoning: Byron Bay is an expensive coastal tourist town in New South Wales. Food and drink are priced like Sydney or Brisbane or a little higher. Accommodation is set like a busy resort town, similar to Noosa, with fewer budget rooms than big cities.
